clusters.name: Cross-layer DSH integration contract drift
clusters.leverage: VERY_HIGH: one cluster blocks three foundational static integration guards across contract, backend, four mobile surfaces and database binding.
clusters.comparisonBasis: Highest proven execution leverage: exact candidate currently fails backend API binding, frontend feature binding and runtime-real-bindings; downstream runtime proof cannot be trusted until these graph edges converge.

clusters.name: Financial presentation bypass of WLT money kernel
clusters.leverage: HIGH but bounded: removes a parallel financial presentation/conversion path in protected finance-facing surfaces.
clusters.comparisonBasis: Finance risk is high, but exact WLT runtime inspection disproved broader assumed sovereignty failures; the proven blast radius is two presentation consumers and is narrower than RC-001.
independenceEvidence: RC-002 touches financial presentation consumers and WLT shared money kernel, not RC-001 contract/router/migration graph files.

clusters.name: Mobile runtime dependency coherence drift
clusters.leverage: MEDIUM_HIGH: one normalized dependency graph removes deterministic mobile bundle-budget drift across all four mobile apps and reduces unused package surface.
clusters.comparisonBasis: Crosses every mobile runtime but does not currently outrank contract/financial authority failures; exact version splits and normal-Knip dependency candidates are known.
independenceEvidence: RC-003 is package-manifest/lockfile scoped and does not overlap RC-001 business contract/router/migration files or RC-002 money-rendering code.

clusters.name: Dead stale and noise inventory not reconciled to real consumers
outcomes: reduced repository noise without removing dynamic entry points
clusters.leverage: MEDIUM: cleanup lowers ambiguity and duplicate/stale authority risk, but strict diagnostics include entry-point-sensitive candidates that cannot be blindly removed.
clusters.comparisonBasis: Normal Knip proves two direct unused files; strict backlog needs graph triage, so cleanup cannot outrank deterministic integration/finance/mobile blockers.

clusters.name: Candidate proof and governance provenance lag live implementation
consumers: all product surfaces relying on closure claims
clusters.leverage: SYSTEM_WIDE at closure: prevents stale governance from masquerading as live truth and prevents narrower contextual CI from being reused as full-workspace proof.
clusters.comparisonBasis: System-wide but downstream for mutation order: current failed source guards must be fixed before registries can truthfully advance; updating proof metadata first would encode false readiness.

selectedFrontier.justification: RC-001 is the highest-ranked executable systemic root because it fails three foundational integration guards across contract, backend, four product surfaces and database migration binding. RC-002/RC-003 are semantically independent but intentionally serialized under one remote writer; RC-005 is downstream of source convergence and exact-candidate proof.
